newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire army pulls back as rebels march on Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army pulls back as rebels march on Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire's army is retreating in the face of a relentless rebel advance on the capital Kinshasa, residents of a town in their path said on Thursday.
Residents of Kenge, just 200 km (125 miles) from the capital, said that the town was calm and waiting for the rebels to arrive -- a familiar pattern in the seven-month campaign.
Zairean soldiers had been retreating through Kenge over the past couple of days, the residents, contacted from Kinshasa, added.
One said soldiers had left the town, a second said only a handful remained.

Laurent Kabila's rebels, who took up arms in October, say they expect to take the capital over the next 10 to 15 days. They now control over a half of the sprawling Central African nation -- including all its main cities outside the capital.

Kabila is expected to hold his first face-to-face meeting with President Mobutu Sese Seko on Saturday on a South African navy ship in international waters in the Atlantic off the coast of Central Africa.
The rebel leader has said he would only discuss terms of Mobutu's departure after 32 years in power. He warned his forces would take the capital if the president does not leave peacefully.
Residents of Kikwit, the rebels forward base for their march on Kinshasa, said an expected rebel airlift into the town had not begun but that reinforcements had been arriving by truck.

Kabila said on Wednesday that Mobutu's army had begun blowing up bridges to try to slow the military push. "They have started blowing up bridges in Kenge in order to stop our forces from advancing to Kinshasa," he told Reuters.
The Kenge residents said they they had no such information.
A mining expert who arrived in the rebel-held southern city of Lubumbashi from the area on Thursday said the rebels were advancing from the towns of Ilebo, Tshikapa, Kananga and Kikwit.

The expert, who declined to be identified, said rebels from Ilebo and Kananga were advancing on foot while those from Tshikapa and Kikwit were using tanks and armoured troop carriers and had long-range artillery pieces and bridge-laying equipment.

"It's big stuff. These guys are heavily equipped and should have no problems crossing the rivers in that area to Kenge and Kinshasa because they are equipped with bridge-laying gear and speedboats," he added.
The rebels predict the fall of Kinshasa in two weeks. The expert agreed: "From what I saw, that timescale makes a lot of sense. These guys are serious."
